issues: Meaning drift in legal citation 16: 'Tambahan Lembaran Negara Republik Indonesia Nomor 64' was translated as 'Supplement ... Number 64' but the original states the State Gazette number is 64 and does not provide a supplement number.

Minor meaning drift/omission in citation 3: the original includes the English title in parentheses '(Convention The Elimination Of All Forms Of Discrimination Againts Women)' (with typos) which is omitted in the translation; downstream legal-indicator matching may rely on this string.
Meaning drift/omission: item 5 in the 'In View of' list omits the Indonesian parenthetical translation '(Konvensi ILO Mengenai Usia Minimum untuk Diperbolehkan Bekerja)'.
Meaning drift/omission: item 12 omits the Indonesian parenthetical translation '(Konvensi Mengenai Hak-Hak penyandang Disabilitas)'.

Meaning drift/omission: item 16 misrenders the citation details; the original states '(State Gazette ... 2006, Supplement ... Number 64)' but the translation renders it as 'State Gazette ... of 2006 Number 64' and omits the 'Supplement' reference.

Scrambled/merged list markers in Articles 2–5: lettered items (a., b., c., d., etc.) are run together (e.g., "andd.", "andc.") and some items are not on their own lines, risking boundary-based parsing errors.

Meaning drift in Article 3: original has items a, b, and c (with "dan" before c), but the translation omits item d and merges content; needs to reflect original lettering sequence (a, b, c) and keep each item distinct.
Minor meaning/term issue: Article 2 principles should be rendered as four separate items a–d; current text merges "dan" with "d" ("andd") which can be misread as part of content rather than a marker.

Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 2: original has inline markers 'a.' 'b.' 'c.' and 'd.' (with 'dan d.' merged as 'dand.'), but translation reformats into a clean vertical list, changing the marker structure used for downstream splitting.

Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 3: original has 'a.' then 'b.' then 'dan c.' but markers are merged inline ('b.' attached to previous clause; 'danc.'), while translation reformats into a clean vertical list, altering marker placement/structure.
Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 4: original ends with 'danh. pendanaan' (h. merged), while translation reformats into a clean vertical list, changing marker structure.

Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 5: original has inline merged markers ('b.' attached to previous clause; 'dand.'), while translation reformats into a clean vertical list, altering marker placement/structure.

Scrambled/merged list markers in several places: missing line breaks cause markers to run together (e.g., Article 6 c./d., Article 8 a./b./c., Article 9 c./d., Article 10 b./c., Article 12 j./k./l. and paragraph (2) a./b., Article 13 a./b. and i./j., Article 14 a./b./c., Article 15(2) a./b./c./d., Article 17 g./h., Article 18(3)/(4)). This risks downstream boundary splitting.
Meaning drift: Article 6(b) translates 'pengelola' (managers/administrators) as 'management' (concept) rather than the people managing/administrating.

Broken/scrambled list formatting in Article 6: item d is separated from the preceding line and the original has a merged 'c...; dan d...' sequence that should be rendered as separate c. and d. items without an extra blank line.

Meaning drift in Article 6(c): original refers to strengthening the capacity of the PUG institution and children (gender mainstreaming and child institution), but translation renders it as 'PUG and children institutions' (plural) which is less faithful; adjust to 'PUG and child institution' wording.

Scrambled numbering/marker placement in Article 12: paragraph (2) marker is detached from the end of paragraph (1) and should appear as a separate numbered paragraph immediately after (1) without extra separation; also ensure list markers a–l remain continuous without unintended paragraph breaks.
Scrambled/missing list structure: in Article 26, paragraph marker “(2)” is not preserved as a separate numbered item and is merged into paragraph (1).
Broken Markdown/list structure: in Article 30, “Article 31” is missing as a heading (####) and is incorrectly appended to Article 30 paragraph (3).

Broken/scrambled list structure: in Article 23 the original has "dan d. hukum" (and d. law) but the translation renders "and d. law"; the list marker "d." must appear as "d." (not "and d.") to preserve exact item boundaries.
Meaning drift: Article 27 incorrectly refers to "Article 22 letter d"; the original refers to "Pasal 23 huruf d" (Article 23 letter d).
Scrambled/merged list markers in Article 34(1): sub-items a–d are run together ("include:a." and "andd.") instead of being clearly separated.
Scrambled/merged list markers in Article 36(1): sub-items a–e are run together ("include: a." and "ande.") instead of being clearly separated.
Scrambled list markers in Article 37: items e, g, and h are merged into the previous items on the same line ("...Victims; e.", "...counselors; g.", "...Victims; h."), breaking list structure.

Broken/scrambled list structure in Article 34(1) and Article 36(1): original has inline list markers (a.–d./e.) immediately after the colon; translation reformats into an indented sublist, which can break downstream boundary matching.

Meaning drift in CHAPTER VIII title: original "PERAN SERTA dan PARTISIPASI MASYARAKAT" is rendered as "COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION and PARTICIPATION" (duplicates 'participation' and omits 'community' as the object of participation).

Broken Markdown structure: the original has a level-5 heading "##### TAMBAHAN LEMBARAN DAERAH KABUPATEN TEMANGGUNG NOMOR 120" after Article 42, but the translation omits the preceding "#### Article 43" heading and its content ("Cukup jelas").
Broken Markdown structure: original ends at '#### Pasal 42' but translation adds an extra heading '#### Article 43' that does not exist in the source.

Meaning/faithfulness issue: '#### Pasal 19' contains typo 'C0ukup jelas' (with zero) in the original; translation normalizes it to 'Sufficiently clear' instead of reflecting the source text exactly (should be kept as-is for strict downstream matching).
